requirements.requirement: Provide a persistent HTTP forward proxy on node1 TCP port 3128 for use by node2.
requirements.summary: The proxy service was enabled and active on node1, listened on 0.0.0.0:3128, accepted successful requests from node2, and recovered after node1 restarted with a different boot identity.

requirements.requirement: Permit proxy requests only to the approved node2 origin on TCP 8081 and reject other destination ports, including CONNECT tunnels.
requirements.summary: Runtime tests from node2 returned HTTP 200 for the approved node2:8081 URL, HTTP 403 for node2:8080 and another host, and proxy HTTP 403 for CONNECT. The allowed and denied behaviors were observed again after restarts.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the staged legacy origin application and make its approved handbook reachable through the proxy from node2.
requirements.summary: Both staged files retained their baseline SHA-256 hashes. The origin service was enabled, active, and listening on 8081; direct and proxied requests returned the approved handbook before and after node2 restarted with a different boot identity.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 after implementation and restart. The services ran using the installed Python 2.7.5 runtime, with no package installation or OS/kernel replacement shown.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The proxy and origin were functional, destination restrictions and CONNECT rejection were directly exercised, staged content was preserved, and both nodes recovered correctly from mandatory restarts without changing RHEL or kernel versions. Only minor temporary evidence-file residue detracts from operational hygiene.
limitations: Package-manager health checks timed out before preparation and after execution, so package consistency could not be independently assessed.

The universal rejection of every non-8081 destination port is supported by the captured proxy enforcement code and representative runtime denial on port 8080; exhaustive testing of all possible ports was not captured.

The proxy script compilation check in cmd-2a5fc843293949dd encountered permission denial while attempting to write a .pyc despite printing a success label; running service and post-restart behavior provide the relevant functional evidence instead.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node2

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive persistent mutations—the two service definitions, proxy implementation, service enablement, and source-scoped firewall rules—had clear task roles. Both mandatory restart protocols were complete and independently corroborated by changed lifecycle boot identities; recovered services, listeners, content, and policy behavior were directly observed. No unrelated troubleshooting mutation was established. The hygiene deduction is for low-risk abandoned evidence residue: node1 retained /tmp/local-proxy-check.out and /tmp/harbor-reboot.log; node2 retained /tmp/harbor-reboot.log plus proxy test output/error files from initial, pre-restart, post-node1-restart, post-node2-restart, and final checks. These files remained at the final snapshot and were not cleaned, although their creation supported bounded verification. Expected systemd-private directories and the required 3128/8081 listeners were not penalized.
